book.title: What this is
book.text:
This app is practice for the written permit test -- the knowledge test you
sit before you can get a learner's permit. It is written from your state's own
driver's manual: every rule here comes out of the manual that state publishes,
one rule at a time, with the reason behind it and a question on it while it is
still fresh.

It is not official. It is not made by, affiliated with or endorsed by any
state's MVA, DMV or licensing authority. It is practice material, and where
this app and your state's handbook disagree, the handbook is right and this
app is not. Passing every test in here is not a guarantee of passing the real
one, and the Terms of use say so.

What makes it different from a bank of random questions: every question is
attached to the rule it tests and the reason that rule exists, so a wrong
answer sends you back to something you can read rather than to a score you
cannot act on.

book.title: Which states, and where a state's numbers are
book.text:
The first screen has a picker: type or choose your state from the list. Only
the states listed there are offered, and each one is written from that
state's own manual.

Every state has its own page, which says which manual it is written from,
which agency publishes it, when it was last checked against it, how many
questions the state's test asks and the score that passes it -- and, for
states that time the test, how long you get. Once you have chosen a state, the
menu has a group named after that state's test; in it, a page about that
state's test has the same facts, plus how the test is given and what you need
to get your permit, and *Key numbers* (in Spanish *Números clave*) is a printable page of every rule
in that state's handbook that comes down to a number. This book does not
repeat those figures: they are different for every state and that page is
where they are.

Where the state publishes no question count or pass mark, the practice test
uses a figure of its own and the page says so; where the pass mark follows
from rules the state does publish, the page says that too.

book.title: The first screen
book.text:
After the picker there are two doors. *Take a 10-question test* (in Spanish *Haga una prueba de 10 preguntas*) is the main one:
a short test drawn from the whole of your state's material, so somebody who
searched for a practice test meets one straight away. *or start studying* (in Spanish *o empiece a estudiar*) is the
second, and opens the first section's questions, with its cards to follow.

Under the doors, *Why this one* (in Spanish *Por qué este*) gives three reasons -- written from
the state's own manual, one payment with no subscription, no account and no
name -- and *What this is* (in Spanish *Qué es esto*) says how this differs from a bank of random
questions and what it covers. At the very bottom of the screen a footer links
to the Terms, the Privacy page, the FAQ, this box, *About* (in Spanish *Quiénes somos*) and the
*Contact us* (in Spanish *Contáctenos*) page.

The menu button is in the top corner of every screen. The language switch,
where a state has Spanish, is on the first screen and in the menu's Settings.

book.title: Studying, one card at a time
book.sources: src/screens/Study.tsx, src/screens/Prescreen.tsx, src/screens/Checkpoint.tsx, src/screens/SectionMap.tsx, docs/plans/ask-first.md, docs/plans/first-sitting.md
book.text:
Each law is one card. Under the card, *Quiz me* (in Spanish *Pregúnteme*) asks a multiple-choice
question on that law. Get it right and you move on to the next card. Get it
wrong and the correct answer is marked, the reason behind the rule is shown,
and the same law comes back until you have it -- there is no skipping a card
you got wrong. Answer choices are shuffled every time, so positions cannot be
memorised.

The cards are grouped into sections, and every section opens on its
questions before its cards: you are asked each law's question first. A right
answer means you already know that law and its card is skipped; a wrong
answer shows you the right one and the card is taught afterwards as it would
have been anyway. Answering before being taught is what makes the rule stick,
and the screen says that you will get most of them wrong and that this is
fine. If you would rather read first, *Skip to the cards* (in Spanish *Ir a las tarjetas*) opens the section's
cards in the usual order; answers already given stand.

At the end of a section a checkpoint names the topics you have just finished,
counts the ones you already knew, and offers *Keep going* (in Spanish *Seguir*). The bar
across the top of every study screen says which section you are in; at a
checkpoint, tapping the pass bar opens the section map, a list of every topic
in your state -- green where the pass has been, grey where it has not. Tapping
a green one walks every card of that topic again; tapping a grey one lets you
be tested out of it.

Where a question has a road sign in it, the sign is drawn on the card. Where
a card has a picture, it is shown. The manual page each rule comes from is
named under the answer.

book.title: The short course and the full course
book.text:
There are two ways through the cards, and you choose on the first card and
can change your mind from the control under the section label or on the hub --
at any time outside a test, a restudy walk or a results screen. The full course is every law, card by card. The short course is
one or two laws on every topic -- far fewer cards, and the card count for
each is shown on the control, because it is your state's own count.

Switching loses nothing: cards you have already studied stay studied, and you
land on the first card the new course still owes you. The tests do not shrink
with the course. A practice test is always drawn from the whole of your
state's material on either course, so on the short course you will meet laws
on a test that you were never shown, and the section map is where you go to
study a topic you want more of.

book.title: The short test
book.text:
The 10-question test is free, needs no sign-up and can be
taken from the first screen, from a study card (*Try 10 sample questions* (in Spanish *Pruebe 10 preguntas de muestra*), from the
whole of your state's test) and again afterwards. The first run
draws 10 questions from all of your state's laws -- a
starting point, not a grade. A retake starts with the laws you missed and the
cards you have studied since, then fills from the rest -- a check on what you
just fixed, not a fresh sample.

The results screen shows your recent runs in a row, so a score that moved is
visible as having moved, and names the topics your misses point at, most
missed first, with a short walk of study cards over them. You can walk out of
a run part-way, back to the card it was opened from or to the hub; it is
dropped, not saved.

It is not your state's paper and is never scored against it. It cannot earn
a level, and it does not count towards Prepared.

book.title: The full practice tests
book.text:
A full practice test is shaped like your state's real one: the same number
of questions and the same pass mark wherever the state publishes them, and
scored in parts where the state scores in parts. Where the state publishes no
count, a count chosen from the state's own rules is used and the screen says
so. The questions are drawn from every law in your state, weighted by what
you have shown: what you missed last time first, then what you have never
answered right, then the rest.

Once you have paid, *Take the test* (in Spanish *Hacer el examen*) is on the hub and on every study
card. After a run with misses, a screen before the next test offers
*Retest the ones you missed* (in Spanish *Repetir las que falló*) as well as *Fresh full test* (in Spanish *Examen completo nuevo*). Where your state times its
test, the switch under the level meter on the hub and in the menu's
*Settings* (in Spanish *Ajustes*) runs the clock for the real number of minutes; during a
timed run *Stop the clock* (in Spanish *Parar el reloj*) turns it off, and if time runs out anything you
did not reach counts as missed, as it does on the real paper. From the menu,
*Start this test over* (in Spanish *Empezar este examen otra vez*) abandons the run in progress and draws a fresh paper.

After a test, the results show each part's score where there are parts,
whether you passed, how many questions short you were if not, and the
questions you missed with the law behind each.

book.title: Green Light, Cruise Control and Prepared
book.sources: src/exam.ts (READY_STREAK, LEVELS), src/screens/Hub.tsx, the test-flow spec
book.text:
Three levels, earned by passing full practice tests in a row. Green Light is
one test passed. Cruise Control is two passed in a row. Prepared is
three full tests passed in a row, and it is the bar: one
pass predicts about a three-in-four chance on the day, three
in a row about nine in ten. The hub shows the level you hold, how many more
passes the next one needs, and the date you reached Prepared.

The passes have to be back to back. A failed run restarts the count, and the
results screen says so. A failed run never takes away a level you have
already earned. A retest of only the questions you missed is too short to
mean what a full run means, so it neither builds the streak nor breaks it.
The 10-question test does not count either way. Where
your state times its test, only timed full runs count towards a level; a run
with the clock off neither builds the streak nor breaks it.

Reaching Prepared is this app's judgement that the work is done. It is not a
promise that you will pass the real exam; what the app promises instead is
the refund described under *The guarantee*.

book.title: Retests, restudy and what you have mastered
book.sources: src/exam.ts (MASTERY_TARGET, MASTERY_DECAY_DAYS, RESTUDY_LIMIT), src/screens/Results.tsx, src/screens/Hub.tsx, src/screens/WalkDone.tsx
book.text:
After a run with misses you can retest exactly the questions you missed, or
take a fresh full test. The results screen also offers *Restudy what you missed* (in Spanish *Repasar lo que falló*):
a short walk of study cards over the topics your misses point at, most missed
first, at most 5 topics, ending back where you were. The hub
keeps a *Worth another look* (in Spanish *Vale la pena repasar*) list of the topics your recent tests say you are
weakest on, with the same walk behind it.

A question you have answered right two times in a row
counts as mastered and stops being drawn ahead of the others, so repeat runs converge on
what you do not know yet. After 10 days a mastered question
comes back into the rotation, because knowing something once is not the same
as knowing it on the day. The hub counts your mastered questions and never
shows a total to reach: it says what you know, not what you are failing to
know.

book.title: What is free, and what the payment is
book.text:
The 10-question test and the first section of study cards are
free, with no sign-up and no account -- on either course, since the free part
is a fixed amount of material rather than a number of pauses. The checkpoint
at the end of the free part says so, and *Keep going* (in Spanish *Seguir*) from it shows
the price. The price is also offered on the results of the short test.

After that, everything is one payment: all the sections of study cards, every
law the exam can ask, unlimited full practice tests, retests built from what
you missed, and every level up to Prepared. It is one payment, not a
subscription -- nothing renews, there is nothing to cancel, and no reminder
to set. The amount is shown before you pay and is lower if a driving school
sent you their link or you have a discount code, which is why no figure is
written here.

book.title: Paying, the recovery code and your devices
book.text:
Payment is handled by Stripe on Stripe's own checkout page; this app never
sees your card details. There is no account and nothing to sign into. When
you come back from checkout you are shown a receipt with a *recovery code*,
and the screen says to write it down: it is the only way back in on another
phone or browser, or if you clear this one, and it is not emailed to you.

To open your purchase on another device, go to the price screen there, tap
*I already paid* (in Spanish *Ya pagué*), enter the recovery code and tap *Restore my purchase* (in Spanish *Recuperar mi compra*). A code
works on up to 5 devices; past that the screen says so and asks
you to use one of the devices already linked or write to us. If you lose the
code, write to joelstevick@gmail.com.

A discount code from a driving school is entered on the price screen, and a
school's link applies its discount for you. Your study progress is separate
from the purchase: it lives on the device you studied on and is not moved by
the code.

book.title: The guarantee, and how a refund works
book.text:
If you do the work and still fail the real exam, you get your money back.
Three conditions, and the first is the one that is really a condition: you
reached Prepared in here first (three full tests passed in a
row); you sat the real exam and wrote to us within 21 days
of paying; and you send a photo of your official result showing your name and
the date -- a phone photo is fine.

Email refund@howardslantern.com with the photo and the recovery code from your receipt;
the code is the only thing that identifies your purchase, since there are no
accounts. What comes back is what you paid less the card processing fee,
which the card company keeps even when a payment is returned. Your access
ends when the refund is made.

The guarantee covers the app in English only. The language the app is in when
you pay is the one that decides: a purchase made with the app in Spanish is
not covered. The Terms of use carry the binding wording, and the
*Request a refund* (in Spanish *Pedir un reembolso*) page in the menu's *Get in touch* (in Spanish *Comuníquese*) group repeats the steps.

book.title: Spanish
book.text:
The language switch is on the first screen, on a state's page and in the
menu's *Settings* (in Spanish *Ajustes*). For a state whose cards have been translated, the
cards, the questions and the app's own screens are in Spanish; for a state
that has not been translated yet, the switch says so in Spanish and the app
stays in English.

Numbers, units and proper names are the same in both languages. The Terms of
use and the Privacy page stay in English with a Spanish summary above them,
and the pass-or-refund guarantee covers purchases made with the app in
English only -- the Spanish price screen does not offer it.

book.title: Settings, read aloud and motion
book.text:
The menu's *Settings* (in Spanish *Ajustes*) group has the timed-test switch (shown with the
real number of minutes, where your state times its test), the course control,
a motion switch that turns animations off, and the language switch.
*Home* (in Spanish *Inicio*) at the top of the menu goes back to the first screen, so a
wrong state is never a trap.

Read aloud is the speaker button at the top of a study or test screen, on the
opposite side of the row from the menu button: switched on, the app reads
each card and question out, and a *Read again* (in Spanish *Leer otra vez*) button beside the
words repeats it. Where the device cannot speak the language on show, the
button is greyed out.

book.title: Starting over
book.text:
*Start over* (in Spanish *Empezar de nuevo*) in the menu forgets everything this device has learned:
how far through the cards you are, which laws you have mastered, every
practice test and the streak they built. You begin at the first card again.
It asks before it does anything, because progress is kept on this device and
nowhere else, so there is no copy for us to put back.

A purchase is not progress and is not affected: if you have paid, you keep the
tests you bought. To abandon the test in progress and draw a fresh one
without touching anything else, use *Start this test over* (in Spanish *Empezar este examen otra vez*).

book.title: What is collected, and what this box keeps
book.text:
There is no account and this app has never asked for your name. Your
progress lives on your device. What is sent is a list of named events -- the
app opened, a state chosen, a card answered and whether you got it right, a
test started and finished, a level earned, the price shown, and the others
the Privacy page lists, each with what travels with it and why it is counted.
They carry two random ids made up on this device -- one for what you do and
one a purchase is attached to -- so what you practise and what you bought can
be read together; neither is a name. Which card you answered and whether you
got it right is sent so badly written cards can be found; never which answer
you picked. The person whose link you arrived on, if any, can see the same
for the people who used that link.

The feedback button in the top corner opens a form with a rating, whether you
have taken the real exam, and an optional comment; a recovery code or an id
pasted into the comment is removed before it is stored, and an email address
you type is kept because a person reads feedback and may reply.

This box keeps what you type for 180 days, without your name or
any id, along with the answer you were shown and the language, so the book it
answers from can be improved. Phone numbers, codes and email addresses are
removed before it is stored or sent anywhere. Your question, the earlier turns
of the same conversation, this book and the FAQ are sent to the company that
runs the model, and nothing else about you. A conversation here runs to
10 questions.

book.title: Who makes this, and how to reach us
book.text:
A small team, named with photographs on the *About us* (in Spanish *Quiénes somos*) page in the
menu's *About this app* (in Spanish *Acerca de esta aplicación*) group. To reach a person, use the *Contact us* (in Spanish *Contáctenos*)
page -- the *Contact* link in the footer, or the first row of the menu's
*Get in touch* (in Spanish *Comuníquese*) group -- which takes your email address and a message and
sends it to us; a lost recovery code goes there too, or to joelstevick@gmail.com
directly. A refund request goes to refund@howardslantern.com. *Send feedback*, on the
front of the menu, is the quickest way to tell us something is wrong with a
card.

book.title: Driving schools and instructors
book.text:
A driving instructor or school can become a partner. They send their students
their own link; a student who studies on it pays less than they otherwise
would, and sees the school's name at the top of every screen where the school
has asked to be named. The school can see how each student is getting on --
whether they have started, which cards they get wrong, and whether they have
passed a practice test -- as a browser shown by a number and its town, or by
the first name or initials the school typed when it invited them; never the
answer you picked. The partner page, at #partner, explains the program,
publishes the whole agreement, and takes applications. A student can use the app without the link and nothing they do
is counted against anybody's code.

book.title: What this box can and cannot answer
book.text:
This box answers questions about how the app works -- what is free, what the
payment opens, how the tests and levels work, how to move a purchase, how a
refund works, what is collected. The answers are written by a model from this
book and the FAQ, and the app checks that every number in an answer is in the
sections it drew on; it can still be wrong, and the pages it links to are what
count.

It answers road law -- what a sign means, a speed limit, a fine, an age -- only
from the laws of the manual of the state you chose, and shows the page of the
manual each answer comes from, as the cards do. Where the manual is silent and
your state's code has been added, it answers from the code instead, and says
so: the answer is marked as not in your manual and names the section. With no state chosen it asks
you to choose one; when your state's manual does not say, it says so rather
than guess. Your state's page has the test's numbers. It does not quote a
price, which is shown before checkout, and it does not
promise that you will pass or that a refund will be approved. For anything it
cannot answer, the *Contact us* (in Spanish *Contáctenos*) page reaches a person, or write to
joelstevick@gmail.com.

faq.question: Is this the official test?
faq.answer: No. This is practice written from your state’s own driver’s manual, not an app made or endorsed by any MVA or DMV — the Terms say so in their first line.

faq.question: Which states can I study for?
faq.answer: The ones listed on the first screen. Each is written from that state’s own manual, and its page says which edition and when it was last checked.

faq.question: How does it work?
faq.answer: You study the law one card at a time, then take practice tests shaped like your state’s real one. Pass one for Green Light, two in a row for Cruise Control, and three full tests in a row for Prepared.

faq.question: Is it in Spanish?
faq.answer: Yes, for the states whose cards have been translated — the language switch is on the first screen and in the menu. The pass-or-refund guarantee covers the app in English only, as the Terms explain.

faq.question: What can I do before paying?
faq.answer: The first section of study cards and the short test are free, with no sign-up. After that, everything is one payment: all the sections, unlimited full tests, retests on what you missed and every level.

faq.question: What does it cost?
faq.answer: One payment, and the price is shown to you before checkout. It is not a subscription — there is nothing to cancel and nothing that renews.

faq.question: What do I get?
faq.answer: Every study card for your state, unlimited full practice tests, retests built from the questions you missed, and every level up to Prepared.

faq.question: Do I need an account?
faq.answer: No. After paying you get a recovery code on your receipt, and it moves your purchase to up to 5 devices — keep it, because it is not emailed to you.

faq.question: What if I fail the real exam?
faq.answer: Reach Prepared here, sit the real exam within 21 days of paying, and send us a photo of your result: we refund what you paid less the card fee. Request a refund has the details.

faq.question: What do you collect about me?
faq.answer: Anonymous counts of what happens in the app, with no account and no name; the only email we hold is one you write to us from, or the one you give Stripe when you pay. The Privacy page lists every one.

faq.question: Who makes this?
faq.answer: A small team, named with faces on About us. To reach us, use the Contact page.

faq.question: I teach driving or run a school.
faq.answer: Your students can study under your name, and you see how they are getting on. Become a partner explains how.

faq.question: Can I ask more questions than the week allows?
faq.answer: Yes: a pack of question tokens from the ask page buys more, where a token is a question about one state and a nationwide question is five. The packs are priced before checkout and in the Terms; tokens do not expire, and an unused pack is refundable.

faq.question: Can a school or a teacher buy questions for a class?
faq.answer: Yes: buy a pack and share its code with the class, typed under I have a code on each device to spend from one balance. Stripe’s receipt carries the business name for expensing, and an unused pack is refundable — Request a refund says how.

faq.question: ¿Es este el examen oficial?
faq.answer: No. Es práctica escrita a partir del manual de manejo de su estado, no una aplicación hecha ni respaldada por ningún MVA o DMV — los Términos lo dicen en su primera línea.

faq.question: ¿Para qué estados puedo estudiar?
faq.answer: Los que aparecen en la primera pantalla. Cada uno está escrito a partir del manual de ese estado, y su página dice qué edición y cuándo se revisó por última vez.

faq.question: ¿Cómo funciona?
faq.answer: Usted estudia la ley una tarjeta a la vez y luego toma exámenes de práctica con la forma del examen real de su estado. Apruebe uno para Luz verde, dos seguidos para Control de crucero y tres exámenes completos seguidos para Preparado.

faq.question: ¿Está en español?
faq.answer: Sí, para los estados cuyas tarjetas se han traducido — el cambio de idioma está en la primera pantalla y en el menú. La garantía de aprobar o recibir un reembolso cubre solo la aplicación en inglés, como explican los Términos.

faq.question: ¿Qué puedo hacer antes de pagar?
faq.answer: La primera sección de tarjetas y el examen corto son gratis, sin registrarse. Después, todo es un solo pago: todas las secciones, exámenes completos sin límite, repasos de lo que falló y todos los niveles.

faq.question: ¿Cuánto cuesta?
faq.answer: Un solo pago, y el precio se le muestra antes de pagar. No es una suscripción — no hay nada que cancelar ni nada que se renueve.

faq.question: ¿Qué recibo?
faq.answer: Todas las tarjetas de su estado, exámenes completos de práctica sin límite, repasos hechos con las preguntas que falló y todos los niveles hasta Preparado.

faq.question: ¿Necesito una cuenta?
faq.answer: No. Después de pagar recibe un código de recuperación en su recibo, y con él pasa su compra a hasta 5 dispositivos — guárdelo, porque no se le envía por correo.

faq.question: ¿Y si no apruebo el examen real?
faq.answer: La garantía cubre solo compras hechas con la aplicación en inglés: llegar a Preparado, presentar el examen real dentro de 21 días de pagar y enviarnos una foto del resultado. Pedir un reembolso tiene los detalles.

faq.question: ¿Qué datos recogen sobre mí?
faq.answer: Conteos anónimos de lo que pasa en la aplicación, sin cuenta y sin nombre; el único correo que guardamos es el que usted usa para escribirnos o el que le da a Stripe al pagar. La página de Privacidad los nombra todos.

faq.question: ¿Quién hace esto?
faq.answer: Un equipo pequeño, con nombres y caras en Quiénes somos. Para comunicarse, use la Página de contacto.

faq.question: Enseño a manejar o tengo una escuela.
faq.answer: Sus estudiantes pueden estudiar bajo su nombre, y usted ve cómo avanzan. Hágase socio explica cómo.

faq.question: ¿Puedo hacer más preguntas de las que permite la semana?
faq.answer: Sí: un paquete de créditos de preguntas desde la página de preguntas da más, donde un crédito es una pregunta sobre un estado y una pregunta para todo el país cuesta cinco. Los paquetes tienen su precio antes de pagar y en los Términos; los créditos no caducan, y un paquete sin usar se reembolsa.

faq.question: ¿Puede una escuela o un maestro comprar preguntas para una clase?
faq.answer: Sí: compre un paquete y comparta su código con la clase, escrito en Tengo un código en cada dispositivo para gastar de un mismo saldo. El recibo de Stripe lleva el nombre del negocio para rendir el gasto, y un paquete sin usar se reembolsa — Pedir un reembolso explica cómo.
